title: Peek shortcut "Space" intermittently fails in File Explorer.
author: tianyixin

confidence.rationale: The symptom pattern strongly implicates the single-space foreground-eligibility cache, but the exact Explorer window-handle transition still needs focused validation.

linked_work.relevance: Recent Peek keyboard-hook change that introduced more complex hotkey handling around focus state.
Earlier Space-key suppression fix during Explorer rename; useful contrast because the current failure is the opposite direction.

judgment.rationale: The default Space shortcut intermittently fails only in File Explorer, not on the Desktop, and immediately recovers after foreground changes such as minimize/restore or switching apps. That pattern aligns with the current single-space activation path in peek/dllmain.cpp, which relies on a cached foreground-eligibility bit updated by a debounced foreground hook instead of recomputing synchronously when the hotkey fires.
evidence: The issue says Space fails intermittently in File Explorer, but Desktop activation works normally and Ctrl+Space eliminates the problem.
A new +1 confirms the same behavior on Windows 10 22H2.
peek/dllmain.cpp special-cases the single-Space hotkey and, when the foreground hook is active, trusts the cached g_foregroundEligible value rather than recomputing eligibility on each press.
Minimize/restore, app switching, or opening Command Palette all create foreground transitions that would refresh that cached eligibility value.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep this as an actionable but design-deferred Peek hotkey regression and run one focused maintainer repro/trace before implementation is approved.

fix_assessment.rationale: The likely fix is confined to the Peek hotkey/foreground eligibility path and does not require additional reporter logs before maintainer-side reproduction.

proposed_fixes.title: Make single-Space Peek activation recompute Explorer eligibility instead of trusting stale cache state
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The default single-Space activation path can block itself when the cached foreground eligibility bit falls out of sync with File Explorer’s current top-level window or tab-host state.
plan: When the single-Space path sees cached ineligibility, perform a synchronous foreground/explorer recheck before dropping the hotkey.
Log and tighten the cases where Explorer foreground windows are missed because the ShellWindows HWND or active-tab HWND changed.
Keep the existing typing/rename suppression behavior, but do not require an unrelated foreground transition to recover single-Space activation.
verification: On File Explorer, repeatedly invoke Peek with Space on a selected file and confirm activation no longer intermittently fails.
Confirm Desktop activation still works and typing/rename suppression from the older Space fix is preserved.
Confirm custom shortcuts such as Ctrl+Space remain unaffected.

confidence.rationale: The cached-eligibility path cleanly matches the observed recovery triggers, but a focused trace should still confirm the missed Explorer state.

issue_context.summary: Peek’s default single-Space hotkey intermittently fails in File Explorer but not on the Desktop, and it starts working again after a foreground change or when the shortcut is changed to Ctrl+Space.
known_information: The issue includes clear File Explorer reproduction steps and notes that Desktop activation still works.
Minimizing and restoring File Explorer, switching to another app and back, or opening Command Palette temporarily restores the Space shortcut.
Changing the shortcut from Space to Ctrl+Space removes the problem.
A second user confirmed the same issue on Windows 10 22H2.
inferences: The problem is specific to the single-Space activation path rather than general Peek preview creation.
Foreground eligibility or Explorer window detection is likely getting stale until another app-focus transition forces a refresh.
issue_context.analysis: The report is already reproducible enough to justify a targeted maintainer reproduce action instead of a generic request for logs.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, the new +1 comment, and current labels.
Inspected src/modules/peek/peek/dllmain.cpp, FileExplorerHelper.cs, and the related Peek startup flow in App.xaml.cs.
Checked recent Peek history, including #48293 and the older Space-while-renaming fix #44995, to isolate the regression area.

actions.label: Reproduce intermittent Peek Space activation in Explorer

reproduce.title: Verify single-Space activation recovers only after a foreground transition
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.100.2 or current main with Space as the Peek shortcut
prerequisites: Peek enabled with the default Space shortcut
A File Explorer window with one selectable file and no inline rename or search box focus
setup: Start from Desktop and confirm Space activates Peek there.
Move to File Explorer and select a file in the main list view.
steps: Press Space repeatedly in File Explorer until Peek fails to open.
Without changing the selection, minimize and restore Explorer or switch to another app and back.
Press Space again and observe whether activation resumes immediately.
Change the shortcut to Ctrl+Space and confirm the same file now opens reliably.
reproduce.expected_result: The current regression shows recovery only after a foreground transition; the intended result is reliable single-Space activation in File Explorer without requiring focus tricks.

actions.label: Approve Peek Space-eligibility fix design
actions.note: Keeps the work bounded to the single-Space eligibility and Explorer foreground-detection path.
